body.estimand_functional: \(\psi(y;x,c)=F_{\rho}(y,\bar c;\bar x;P_{\mathrm{obs}})\big/\sum_{y'}F_{\rho}(y',\bar c;\bar x;P_{\mathrm{obs}})\) on a successful branch; on a passing affine failure template, \(E_Tq=0\) and \(b_Tq\neq0\) certify nonidentification.

sampling_model.design: One selected observational law \(P(V\mid S=\mathbf 1)\) generated by a positive discrete SCM represented by an input-free COPAG.
sampling_model.units: Identification compares structural models that induce the same complete selected observational distribution.
sampling_model.treatment: The intervention fixes \(X=x\); legal Rule-2 exchanges may reallocate coordinates between \(X\) and \(C\).
sampling_model.overlap: The published positive discrete model class makes every displayed selected conditioning stratum well defined.
sampling_model.nuisance_estimation: None; the contribution is graphical identification and exact rational certificate synthesis rather than sampling inference.

comparator_promise_table.comparator_claim: The selected conditional procedure is sound, while conditional completeness is left to future work.
A sufficient graphical condition and a sound algorithm address \(P_X(Y\mid S=1)\) in one known augmented ADMG with latent variables.
Discrete causal questions reduce to polynomial programs that yield sharp or epsilon-sharp bounds.
Conditional interventional distributions have a necessary-and-sufficient identification criterion for a specified semi-Markovian graph.
CIDP is sound and complete for conditional causal-effect identification from PAGs without selection.
Graphical and formula-specific positivity conditions can license identifying formulas without global strict positivity.

body.tldr: Branch-sCIDP is a direct published-class soundness specialization and finite formula search, not a new completeness theorem. A general selection-equalizer lift now converts any two positive rational finite SCMs with the same observational law but different ordinary interventional outcome laws into selected models with the same full selected observational law, a common positive conditioning denominator, and different joint numerators and conditional effects. The connected binary table is an exact instance, while the affine rank compiler gives a second exact construction for a supplied represented family. Whether every all-branches failure yields a represented locked construction remains open.

project_justification.gap: Failure of selected joint identification does not by itself preserve the conditioning denominator, and the published conditional algorithm supplies soundness rather than selected conditional completeness. Ordinary selected hedges therefore leave a genuine graph-to-lock construction problem.
project_justification.niche: The paper separates three levels cleanly: the published positive-discrete Branch-sCIDP soundness result, exact algebraic or equalizer constructions of denominator-locked rational witnesses, and the still-open graphical implication from universal branch failure to one of those constructions.
project_justification.fill: The proved contribution is a general constructive selection-equalizer lift, an exact affine rank compiler for a supplied represented model family, and a connected positive rational binary instance with a same-graph perturbation showing that locking is tuned rather than graph-imposed. The residual forest-to-lock implication is retained as an open question.

body.related_work: Chen and Mooij provide the selected-COPAG model, complete unconditional sIDP, and sound conditional sCIDP. Branch-sCIDP is presented only as a direct input-free-COPAG specialization and exhaustive restatement of that published soundness architecture. Their unconditional residual forests motivate the open graph-to-lock question but do not establish denominator locking. Abouei and coauthors study selected hedges for an unconditional selected intervention target in a known augmented graph, whereas the present equalizer and rank constructions coordinate a postintervention conditioning denominator. Shpitser and Pearl and, without selection, Jaber and coauthors provide the fixed-graph and PAG conditional benchmarks that motivate exhaustive role exchange. Duarte and coauthors motivate exact finite discrete fiber computation; the present rational constructions target checkable nonidentification certificates rather than sharp-bound optimization.
body.honest_scope: No selected conditional completeness theorem is claimed. Branch-sCIDP soundness is stated over the published positive discrete class and allows countable discrete coordinate supports; because the observed vertex set is finite, every joint outcome assignment space used in normalization is at most countable. The affine compiler and the explicit tabular witnesses lie unconditionally in the positive rational binary subclass. The generic selection-equalizer lift instead supplies a positive rational finite witness in the published discrete class. Under its common-graph and active-parent hypotheses, the model classes are indexed by the input-free COPAG \(\mathcal P^+\) represented by the selected projection of the common extended graph, rather than by that graph itself. The lift lies in the positive rational binary subclass only when every endogenous and latent variable of each base SCM is binary; the appended private noises can then also be chosen binary. Without that support hypothesis, the lift does not itself yield a binary certificate pair. A countermodel pair in the binary subclass refutes identification in the larger class, but this negative transfer supplies no positive completeness implication. The affine rank equivalence is conditional on a specified perturbation interval that remains in the represented class. The connected table proves nonvacuity and the same-graph perturbation proves that its lock is not structural. The implication from all reachable terminal failures to a represented residual forest with a locked rational pair, together with the advertised synthesis bound, remains exactly the graph-to-lock open question. Continuous variables, intervention inputs, faithfulness-only claims, and general finite-alphabet certificate completeness are outside scope.
